findings.evidence: Lines 136–143 expose `{lambda | ∃ R, IsResolventAt A lambda R}` and immediately restate exactly that body as `mem_resolventSet_iff`.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` and use `mem_resolventSet_iff` wherever membership must be reduced to existence of an inverse.
findings.issue: `resolventSet` is marked `@[expose]` even though `mem_resolventSet_iff` provides its complete public characterization, coupling consumers to the implementation body.

findings.evidence: Both conclusions reduce an inverse composition to its argument; the parallel established API already marks `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolventLeftInv` and `ContractionSemigroup.resolventLeftInv` with `@[simp]` in `Resolvent/Identity.lean` lines 97 and 242.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` to both inverse identities (lines 186 and 191).
findings.issue: The canonical right- and left-inverse normal forms `smul_sub_apply_resolvent` and `resolvent_smul_sub_apply` lack `@[simp]`, so routine resolvent expressions do not normalize through the public API.

summary: The API unnecessarily exposes the resolvent-set implementation and omits simplification attributes on its canonical inverse identities.
